report:
Finding
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward culinary / recipe / food-writing content (especially baking): make continuations more about cooking, kitchens, baking, butter/cake, recipes, chefs, Thanksgiving, etc.

Why (evidence -> reasoning)
1. Strong domain tokens in the logit-lens directions
   - Across many high-norm (layer,position) cells the top vocabulary directions are repeatedly kitchen/cooking words: "Kitchen", "Cook", "Cooking", "Bake", "Baked", "recipes", "recipe", "butter", "cake", "chefs", "culinary", "Chef", "Thanksgiving", "kitchen", "baking", "Bake", "Butter", etc. This is not a scattered theme — the same culinary cluster appears at many layers and positions among the highest-norm cells, which is what you’d expect if the finetune pushes the model to produce food/recipe content.

2. Concentration at early token positions and late layers
   - The L2-norm difference is concentrated in later layers (layers ~11–25, especially 14–25) and primarily at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1 largest). That pattern indicates the finetuning changed the model’s prior / early-token generative steering (how continuations are produced from the start of a prompt), implemented as high-level adjustments in late layers rather than low-level lexical changes. In practice this is consistent with a domain finetune that encourages recipe-style continuations independent of much of the input.

3. Repeated phrase-pattern tokens and supporting words
   - Besides ingredient/technique tokens, tokens like "Remember", "Beyond", "Too", "Showcase", "Family", "creamy", "Hour", "Thanksgiving" point to recipe/article style (tips, time, serving context, holiday recipes). That supports the hypothesis that the finetune targeted cooking/food-blog style writing rather than e.g. a single special token or a safety filter.

Conclusion
- Model B was finetuned to specialize in the culinary/recipe domain (a recipe generator or food-writing persona), causing its residual stream to shift toward tokens and continuations about cooking, baking, and related concepts.
